questions.prompt: What does Anthropic's post say A/B testing measures?

options.text: Actual user outcomes, such as retention and task completion.
options.explanation: Right. It compares variants with real user traffic.

options.text: How well the model scores on a fixed set of test tasks.
options.explanation: That describes an automated eval, not an A/B test.

options.text: How many tokens the model writes in each answer.
options.explanation: Token counts are an operating number, not the outcome an A/B test measures.

questions.prompt: According to Anthropic's post, why is an A/B test slow?

options.text: It needs a new model to be trained for each group.
options.explanation: The post gives a different reason.

options.text: It can run only once the vendor has approved the test.
options.explanation: The post names no vendor approval step.

options.text: It needs days or weeks, and enough traffic.
options.explanation: Right. That is the con the post lists.

questions.prompt: Which method does Anthropic's post say is most useful pre-launch and in CI/CD?

options.explanation: The post says A/B testing validates significant changes once you have sufficient traffic.

options.text: Automated evals, run on each change.
options.explanation: Right. The post calls them the first line of defense against quality problems.

options.text: User feedback buttons in the finished product.
options.explanation: The post lists feedback as an ongoing practice after launch.
